subject: Accounting
title: The Bernie Madoff Ponzi Scheme
description: A quick win: understand The Bernie Madoff Ponzi Scheme.

hook.text: For decades, Bernie Madoff promised steady 10-12% returns. Nobody questioned it—until $65 billion vanished.

buildup.text: Madoff ran the largest Ponzi scheme in history—paying old investors with new investors' money.

discovery.text: Analyst Harry Markopolos warned the SEC repeatedly, proving the returns were mathematically impossible.

twist.text: The SEC investigated and found nothing—multiple times. The fraud only collapsed when the market crashed.

climax.text: Madoff was sentenced to 150 years. Thousands of people lost their life savings in the collapse.

punchline.text: If returns seem too good to be true, they probably are.

quiz.question: Who repeatedly warned the SEC about Madoff's scheme?

details.summary: Bernie Madoff operated the largest Ponzi scheme in history—$65 billion in fabricated gains—for nearly two decades before it collapsed in 2008. This topic examines how the scheme operated, why red flags were ignored, and the forensic lessons from the investigation.
details.whyItMatters: The Madoff case exposed catastrophic failures in SEC oversight and raised fundamental questions about why red flags identified by investigator Harry Markopolos were repeatedly ignored.
takeaways: Madoff paid consistent 10-12% returns regardless of market conditions — impossible for the claimed strategy
Harry Markopolos identified the fraud years earlier and repeatedly alerted the SEC, which failed to act
The scheme collapsed when the 2008 crisis triggered $7 billion in redemption requests Madoff couldn't meet

faq.question: How did Bernie Madoff's Ponzi scheme work?
faq.answer: Madoff accepted investor money but never actually invested it. He paid returns to existing investors using money from new investors, creating the illusion of consistent profits. Fabricated account statements showed steady returns of 10-12% per year regardless of market conditions.

faq.question: Why wasn't Madoff's scheme detected sooner?
faq.answer: The SEC failed to investigate despite multiple detailed complaints from Harry Markopolos. Madoff's reputation as a former NASDAQ chairman lent credibility. Investors didn't question consistent returns. The scheme's feeder funds added layers of apparent legitimacy and social exclusivity.
